scenes.text: Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive, more than a hundred years later.
She was born on November seventh, eighteen sixty-seven, in Warsaw, Poland.
She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the only person to win in two different sciences.
But years of working with radium left her papers, clothes and furniture contaminated.
Today her notebooks are stored in lead-lined boxes at France's national library in Paris.
Radium has a half-life of about sixteen hundred years, so they'll stay radioactive for a very long time.
Would you dare to read them?

title: Marie Curie's notebooks are STILL radioactive ☢️
caption: Marie Curie (born Nov 7, 1867) won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry. Her radium-contaminated notebooks are kept in lead-lined boxes at the Bibliothèque nationale de France. ☢️
